dialogues.title: Dialogue 1
dialogues.setting: A husband and wife agree about the temperature, but not about much else.

lines.speaker: Mr. Wong
lines.zh: 而家天气渐渐冷勒。我好怕冷，我最中意晒太阳嘅。天文台话今日会落雨，呢个星期六仲会落雪添。
lines.jp: ji4 gaa1 tin1 hei3 zim6 zim6 laang5 laak3. ngo5 hou2 paa3 laang5, ngo5 zeoi3 zung1 ji3 saai3 taai3 joeng4 ge3. tin1 man4 toi4 waa6 gam1 jat6 wui2 lok6 jyu5, ni1 go3 sing1 kei4 luk6 zung6 wui5 lok6 syut3 tim1
lines.en: Right now the weather is gradually getting colder. I dislike coldness. I love sunbathing. The observatory said today there will be rain. There will even be snow this Saturday

lines.speaker: Mrs. Wong
lines.zh: 我已经预备咗啲冷天衫啦。
lines.jp: ngo5 ji5 ging1 jyu6 bei6 zo2 di1 laang5 tin1 saam1 laa3
lines.en: I have already prepared winter clothing

lines.speaker: Mr. Wong
lines.zh: 我想听日买个电暖炉返黎，你话好唔好呀？
lines.jp: ngo5 soeng2 ting1 jat6 maai5 go3 din6 nyun5 lou4 faan1 lai4, nei5 waa6 hou2 m4 hou2 aa3?
lines.en: I want to buy an electric heater tomorrow, what do you think?

lines.speaker: Mr. Wong
lines.jp: gam2, ngo5 jiu3 gei2 si4 maai5 aa3?
lines.en: Then, when should I buy it?

lines.speaker: Mrs. Wong
lines.zh: 唔好买电暖炉啦！你买嘅嘢时时都唔实用嘅。
lines.jp: m4 hou2 maai5 din6 nyun5 lou4 laa1! nei5 maai5 ge3 je5 si4 si4 dou1 m4 sat6 jung6 ge3
lines.en: Don't buy the electric heater! The things you bought are often impractical

lines.speaker: Mr. Wong
lines.zh: 我唔同意，我买嘅嘢最实用嘅勒。
lines.jp: ngo5 m4 tung4 ji3, ngo5 maai5 ge3 je5 zeoi3 sat6 jung6 ge3 laak3
lines.en: I don't agree, the things I bought are always the most practical

lines.speaker: Mrs. Wong
lines.zh: 你要知道买唔实用嘅嘢即係嘥钱。
lines.jp: nei5 jiu3 zi1 dou6 maai5 m4 sat6 jung6 ge3 je5 zik1 hai6 saai1 cin2
lines.en: You need to understand buying impractical things is the same as wasting money

lines.speaker: Mr. Wong
lines.zh: 你话我听，我买咗乜嘢唔实用呀？
lines.jp: nei5 waa6 ngo5 teng1, ngo5 maai5 zo2 mat1 je5 m4 sat6 jung6 aa3?
lines.en: Tell me, what did I buy that is impractical?

lines.speaker: Mrs. Wong
lines.zh: 挤喺走廊墙角嗰个手提灭火筒，你旧年买嘅，一年之内都冇用过，你话係唔係唔实用丫！
lines.jp: zai1 hai2 zau2 long4 coeng4 gok3 go2 go3 sau2 tai4 mit6 fo2 tung2, nei5 gau6 nin2 maai5 ge3, jat1 nin4 zi1 noi6 dou1 mou5 jung6 gwo3, nei5 waa6 hai6 m4 hai6 m4 sat6 jung6 aa1!
lines.en: The portable fire extinguisher placed at the corner of the corridor, you bought it last year, we didn't use it within one year, you said isn't it impractical?

questions: Select the correct phrase: Wong4 sin1 saang1 daa2 syun3 maai5 (din6 nyun5 lou4 / mit6 fo2 tung2).
Select the correct phrase: Wong4 taai3 taai2 waa6 Wong4 sin1 saang1 maai5 ge3 je5 si4 si4 dou1 (jau5 jung6 / mou5 jung6 / m4 sat6 jung6).
Select the correct phrase: Go2 go3 sau2 tai4 mit6 fo2 tung2 zai1 hai2 (zau2 lau4 / se2 zi6 lau4 / coeng4 gok3).
Select the correct phrase: Go2 go3 sau2 tai4 mit6 fo2 tung2 (jung6 gwo3 jat1 ci3 / mou5 jung6 gwo3 / si4 si4 jung6).

dialogues.title: Dialogue 2
dialogues.setting: Mr. Chan and Mr. Cheung demonstrate how buying an air conditioner can lead to a conflict of stinginess

lines.speaker: Chan
lines.jp: zoeng1 sin1 saang1, nei5 hou2. heoi3 bin1 cyu3 aa3?
lines.en: Mr. Cheung, hello. Where are you going?

lines.speaker: Cheung
lines.jp: ngo5 heoi3 maai5 laang5 hei3 gei1
lines.en: I'm going to buy an air conditioner

lines.speaker: Chan
lines.zh: 係呀！天气渐渐热，买冷气机係时候啦。
lines.jp: hai6 aa3! tin1 hei3 zim6 zim6 jit6, maai5 laang5 hei3 gei1 hai6 si4 hau6 laa3
lines.en: Right, the weather is getting hotter, this is the right time to buy an air conditioner

lines.speaker: Cheung
lines.zh: 陈先生，你有乜嘢打算呢？
lines.jp: can4 sin1 saang1, nei5 jau5 mat1 je5 daa2 syun3 ne1?
lines.en: Mr. Chan, what are you going to do?

lines.speaker: Chan
lines.zh: 我冇钱买冷气机。天气太热嘅时候，我会去海滩游水，饮啤酒，食雪糕，咁就唔热喇。
lines.jp: ngo5 mou5 cin2 maai5 laang5 hei3 gei1. tin1 hei3 taai3 jit6 ge3 si4 hau6, ngo5 wui5 heoi3 hoi2 taan1 jau4 seoi2, jam2 be1 zau2, sik6 syut3 gou1, gam3 zau6 m4 jit6 laa1
lines.en: I don't have money to buy an air conditioner. When the weather gets too hot, I will go to the beach to swim, drink beer, eat ice cream, then I won't be hot anymore

lines.speaker: Cheung
lines.zh: 但係如果打风就唔可以去海滩，落雨就唔可以去买雪糕……咁，就点呀？冷气机唔算好贵，但係好有用：你都唔买，真係悭勒！
lines.jp: daan6 hai6 jyu4 gwo2 daa2 fung1 zau6 m4 ho2 ji5 heoi3 hoi2 taan1, lok6 jyu5 zau6 m4 ho2 ji5 heoi3 maai5 syut3 gou1 … gam2, zau6 dim2 aa1? laang5 hei3 gei1 m4 syun3 hou2 gwai3, daan6 hai6 hou2 jau5 jung6: nei5 dou1 m4 maai5, zan1 hai6 haan1 laak3!
lines.en: But if there's a typhoon you can't go to the beach, if it rains you can't buy ice cream, then what are you going to do? An air conditioner isn't too expensive, but it's very useful: but you still won't buy it, you are so stingy

lines.speaker: Chan
lines.zh: 我唔算悭啦！我话你太太仲悭喇！
lines.jp: ngo5 m4 syun3 haan1 laa1! ngo5 waa6 nei5 taai3 taai2 zung6 haan1 laa1!
lines.en: I'm not stingy! I think your wife is even more stingy!

lines.speaker: Cheung
lines.jp: keoi5 dim2 joeng2 haan1 faat3 aa3?
lines.en: She is stingy in what way?

lines.speaker: Chan
lines.zh: 呢个礼拜二我喺百货公司买游水裤嘅时候，见到你太太，佢好开心咁话我知，佢只係用咗一条你嘅旧领呔就可以改成一套“比基尼”勒。你话佢悭唔悭呢呀！
lines.jp: ni1 go3 lai5 baai3 ji6 ngo5 hai2 baak3 fo3 gung1 si1 maai5 jau4 seoi2 fu3 ge3 si4 hau6, gin3 dou2 nei5 taai3 taai2, keoi5 hou2 hoi1 sam1 gam2 waa6 ngo5 zi1, keoi5 zi2 hai6 jung6 zo2 jat1 tiu4 nei5 ge3 gau6 leng5 taai1 zau6 ho2 ji5 goi2 sing4 jat1 tou3 "bei2 gei1 nei4" laak3. nei5 waa6 keoi5 haan1 m4 haan1 ne1 aa3!
lines.en: This Tuesday I went to the department store to buy swim trunks, I saw your wife, she told me excitedly, she used your old necktie and alter it to make a set of bikini. You said isn't she stingy!

grammar.title: What's more
grammar.summary: zung6 means furthermore, in addition; it is an adverb placed before the verb and is usually backed up by the final particle tim1.
grammar.body:
仲 zung6 means furthermore, in addition (you met the same word in Unit 3 when it means still, yet). It is an adverb and therefore, as you now know, comes before the verb in the sentence.
The final particle tim1 is usually added on at the end to give additional force to zung6.

examples.jp: ngo5 zung6 jau5 loeng5 go3 tim1
examples.en: I've got two more as well

examples.jp: keoi5 zung6 soeng2 heoi3 mei5 gwok3 jat1 ci3 tim1
examples.en: What's more she wants to go to the States once as well

grammar.title: When?
grammar.summary: gei2 si4? asks for a time-when answer and sits where that answer would go in the sentence.
grammar.body:
gei2 si4? when? is the question word which asks for a time when answer.
You will find gei2 si4? in the same place in the sentence where the time when answer comes.

grammar.title: More on dou1
grammar.summary: dou1 (all, both, also) goes immediately before the verb and is thrown in whenever there is a plural idea or an idea of wholeness.
grammar.body:
都 dou1 is an adverb which means all, both, also and that it is placed like other adverbs immediately in front of the verb. Sometimes it is used where there seems no need for it in English: for instance, in the dialogue Mrs. Wong says nei5 maai5 ge3 je5 si4 si4 dou1 m4 sat6 jung6 ge3 (the things you buy are always impractical). What dou1 is doing is backing up the word si4 si4 always, and it does so because si4 si4 feels like a plural idea in Cantonese - it literally means time-time.
Whenever there are plural ideas (the cows all….; Mr. and Mrs. Wong…; electric heaters…) or ideas of wholeness (the entire population…; the whole busload…) you can expect dou1 to be thrown in for good measure.

examples.jp: keoi5 dei6 cyun4 dou1 hai6 zung1 gwok3 jan4
di1 ngau4 dou1 hai6 sik6 cou2 daai6 ge3

grammar.title: More about most
grammar.summary: zeoi3 makes superlatives; the final particle laak3 is often tagged on to back it up, just as tim1 backs up zung6.
grammar.body:
In Unit 6 we met 最 zeoi3 most and you will have no difficulty in using it to make superlatives (biggest, coldest, best, etc.).
Quite often you will find that the final particle laak3 is tagged onto the sentence to back up zeoi3, just as tim1 backs up zung6.

examples.jp: lou4 si1 loi4 si1 hai6 jing1 gwok3 zeoi3 gwai3 ge3 ce1 laak3
examples.en: The Rolls-Royce is Britain's most expensive car

grammar.title: Tone changes
grammar.summary: nin4 year changes to the high-rising tone nin2 in last year, this year and next year only.
grammar.body:
In the dialogue you will notice that the word for year appears in two different tones. The usual tone is nin4 (low falling), but in last year gau6 nin2 it becomes high-rising. There is no obvious reason why this tone change should occur, but take heart that it only happens in the following common words.
In all other cases year is pronounced in the low falling tone nin4.

grammar.title: Years and days
grammar.summary: nin4 year and jat6 day take no classifier; they combine the roles of classifier and noun.
grammar.body:
When we were talking about nin4, you might note that it is one of a very small number of nouns which do not need a classifier. You have learned that nouns must have a classifier when they are counted or specified with words like this, that and which, so you know that two pens must be loeng5 zi1 bat1 and three Americans must be saam1 go3 mei5 gwok3 jan4.
nin4 year and jat6 day, however, along with one or two other nouns that you have not met, do not have a classifier; they seem to combine the role of classifier and noun at the same time. So one day is jat1 jat6 and two years is loeng5 nin4.

grammar.title: In what way?
grammar.summary: dim2 joeng2 can pair with the verb ending -faat3 way of…; the object then moves to the front of the sentence.
grammar.body:
We first met dim2 joeng2 in what way? how? in Unit 5. In the dialogue we see that it appears with the verb ending -faat3 way of… You do not have to use this new form, but it is quite good racy-sounding Cantonese to do so. Here are two example sentences each using both forms.
When the -faat3 form is used, note how in each case the object of the verb moves to the front of the sentence and the -faat3 tacks onto the verb. There is a useful principle to be learned: Cantonese verbs are sensitive creatures (remember how some of them feel lonely?) And they don't feel happy with too many ideas hanging on them. Verb endings must add directly onto the verb and so if there is an object as well and it makes the verb feel overburdened, it often feels more comfortable to shift that object to the front of the sentence.

examples.jp: keoi5 dim2 joeng2 heoi3 fei1 gei1 coeng4 aa3?
examples.en: How is he going to the airport?

examples.jp: fei1 gei1 coeng4 keoi5 dim2 joeng2 heoi3 faat3 aa3?
examples.en: How is he going to the airport?

examples.jp: keoi5 dim2 joeng2 haan1 cin2 aa3?
cin2 keoi5 dim2 joeng2 haan1 faat3 aa3?

grammar.title: si4 hau6 Time
grammar.summary: hai6 si4 hau6 means it is the right time to…; … ge3 si4 hau6 means when… or while….
grammar.body:
Hai6 si4 hau6 is a colloquial way to say it is the right time to … Here are two ways of using it.
Perhaps more common is the expression … ge3 si4 hau6, which means when… or while… study these two sentences carefully.

examples.jp: ji4 gaa1 hai6 si4 hau6 faan1 se2 zi6 lau4 laa3
examples.en: It's time to go to the office now

examples.jp: ji4 gaa1 faan1 se2 zi6 lau4 hai6 si4 hau6 laa3
examples.en: It's time to go to the office now

examples.jp: ngo5 zyu2 sung3 ge3 si4 hau6 m4 soeng2 maa4 maa1 bong1 ngo5 sau2
examples.en: I don't want mummy to help me while I'm cooking

examples.jp: keoi5 hai2 jing1 gwok3 ge3 si4 hau6 si4 si4 dou1 lai4 taam3 ngo5
examples.en: She often comes to see me when she's in Britain

grammar.title: Making adverbs from adjectives
grammar.summary: Bracketing an adjective with hou2…gam2 turns it into an adverb.
grammar.body: If you bracket an adjective with hou2…gam2 you turn it into an adverb.

examples.jp: keoi5 hou2 nau1 gam2 waa6 ngo5 zi1

grammar.title: -dou2 to succeed in
grammar.summary: The verb ending -dou2 can mean to succeed in, successfully or actually, and often adds little to the verb's meaning.
grammar.body: It is not easy to put a specific meaning on the verb ending -dou2. Sometimes you might want to translate it as to succeed in, sometimes as successfully, sometimes as actually and quite often seems to add nothing much at all to the meaning of the verb to which it is attached. Here are four examples of it with different verbs.

examples.jp: ngo5 tai2 dou2 wong4 siu2 ze2 hai2 go2 cyu3
examples.en: I caught sight of Miss Wong there

examples.jp: ngo5 gu2 dou2 nei5 hai2 cyu4 fong2
examples.en: I guessed rightly that you were in the kitchen

examples.jp: ngo5 gin3 dou2 nei5 taai3 taai3

grammar.title: -sing4 to become
grammar.summary: As a verb ending -sing4 means to become or to make into.
grammar.body: As a verb ending -sing4 means to become or to make into. You will find an example in the dialogue where Mrs. Cheung claims to make a tie into a bikini. Here is another one.

examples.jp: ngo5 jung6 ngau4 juk6 zou6 sing4 jat1 go3 tong1
examples.en: I'm making the beef into a soup

grammar.title: Space and time: prepositions and demonstratives
grammar.summary: Three classes of words express location: prepositions, demonstratives based on ni1 and go2, and localizers.
grammar.body:
3 important classes of words involved in the expression of location.
1. Prepositions.
2. Demonstrative terms based on ni1 'this' and go2 'that'.

grammar.title: Space and time: localizers
grammar.summary: Localizers (postpositions) indicate spatial relationships; bin6 and min6 both mean 'side' and are mostly interchangeable.
grammar.body:
3. Localizers or postpositions indicating spatial relationships.
Bin6 and min6, both meaning 'side' are interchangeable in most cases.

grammar.title: Location (i): hai2 followed by names of places
grammar.summary: hai2 plus a place name states where someone or something is; hai2 dou6 'to be here' is used when presence or absence is at issue.
grammar.body:
Using the words introduced above, several characteristic patterns are used to indicate location in space.
(i) hai2 followed by names of places.
The word hai2 dou6 'to be here' is generally used instead of hai2 ni1 dou6 when presence or absence is at issue. For example on the phone: lei5 sin1 saang1 m4 hai2 dou6 (Mr. Lee is not here).

examples.jp: di1 sai3 lou6 zai2 hai2 go2 dou6
keoi5 dei6 nei1 maai4 hai2 ni1 dou6
ngo5 gam1 jat6 sing4 jat6 hai2 nguk1 kei2
examples.en: I was at home all day today

examples.jp: keoi5 hai2 mei5 gwok3 duk6 syu1
ngo5 dei6 hai2 hok6 haau6 hoi1 wui2
examples.en: We're having a meeting at school

examples.jp: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 m4 hai2 gung1 si1
examples.en: She is not at the office at the moment

examples.jp: lei5 sin1 saang1 m4 hai2 dou6

grammar.title: Location (ii): hai2 together with a localizer
grammar.summary: hai2 can be followed by a localizer, and a noun phrase can come between them in the pattern hai2 (…) X-min6/bin6.
grammar.body:
(ii) hai2 together with a localizer.
A noun phrase can come between hai2 and the localizer, in the pattern hai2 (…) X-min6/bin6.

examples.en: The cinema is just opposite (across the street)

examples.jp: bun2 syu1 hai2 zoeng1 toi2 soeng6 bin6
examples.en: The book is on the table
examples.lit: The book on the table top

examples.jp: keoi5 kei5 hai2 po1 syu6 hau6 min6
examples.lit: She stood at the tree behind

examples.jp: ngo5 zyu6 hai2 keoi5 nguk1 kei5 deoi3 min6
examples.lit: I live at her home opposite

grammar.title: Location: dou6 as a localizer
grammar.summary: dou6 'there' serves colloquially as a localizer after a noun phrase, and is required after nouns like car or computer.
grammar.body:
Dou6 'there' serves colloquially as a localizer in this pattern.
While this pattern with two separate expressions of location may appear redundant, dou6 is required here.

examples.en: The pictures are with me/at my place

examples.jp: keoi5 dei6 hai2 gaa3 ce1 dou6
examples.en: They're in the car (not *keoi5 dei6 hai2 gaa3 ce1)

examples.jp: di1 zi1 liu2 hai2 din2 nou5 dou6
examples.en: The data are in the computer (not *di1 zi1 liu2 hai2 din6 nou5)

grammar.title: Location: zi1 gaan1 and existential patterns
grammar.summary: zi1 gaan1 'between' joins two noun phrases; a demonstrative or localizer can be followed by jau5/mou5 or another verb, optionally with a noun phrase before the localizer.
grammar.body:
With zi1 gaan1 'between', tung4 is used to join the two noun phrases concerned.
A demonstrative form or localizer followed by the existential jau5 or its negative counterpart mou5 or another verb.
A noun phrase can be added before the localizer.

examples.jp: ngo5 tung4 keoi5 zi1 gaan1 mou5 saai3 gam2 cing4
examples.en: There's no feeling left between us
examples.lit: I and him between haven't all feeling

examples.jp: cing4 gam2 tung4 lei5 zi3 zi1 gaan1 hou2 naan4 syun2 zaak6
examples.en: It's difficult to choose between emotion and rationality
examples.lit: Emotion and rationality between very hard to choose

examples.jp: ni1 dou6 jau5 hou2 do1 sai3 lou6 zai2
go2 dou6 mou5 jau4 wing6 ci4
jap6 bin6 jau5 hou2 do1 je5
examples.en: There are lots of things inside

examples.jp: daai6 hok6 leoi5 min6 jau5 saam1 go3 tou4 syu1 gun2
examples.en: There are three libraries in the university

examples.jp: gaan1 fong2 zung1 gaan1 jau5 go3 gong3 kam4
examples.en: There's a piano in the middle of the room

exercises.title: Exercise 1
exercises.instructions: Match the correct Part B with its part A to make meaningful sentences. Part B options: …zik1 hai6 saai1 cin2 / …maai5 laang5 hei3 gei1 hai6 si4 hau6 laa1 / …ngo5 dei6 di1 laang5 tin1 saam1 laa1 / …daan6 hai6 hou2 jau5 jung6

items.answer: tin1 hei3 zim6 zim6 jit6, maai5 laang5 hei3 gei1 hai6 si4 hau6 laa1

items.answer: laang5 hei3 gei1 m4 syun3 hou2 gwai3, daan6 hai6 hou2 jau5 jung6

exercises.title: Exercise 2
exercises.instructions: How can you turn these two sentences into one? Example: go2 cyu3 jau5 ce1. ce1 hou2 gwai3. Answer: go2 cyu3 jau5 hou2 gwai3 ge3 ce1. Try to do the same with the following sentences.

items.prompt: Zoeng1 siu2 ze2 hai6 jat6 bun2 jan4. keoi5 hou2 leng3.
items.answer: Zoeng1 siu2 ze2 hai6 hou2 leng3 ge3 jat6 bun2 jan4
items.answer_en: Miss Cheung is a very pretty Japanese
items.hint: Turn the second sentence into a ge3 modifier before the noun

items.prompt: ngo5 m4 soeng2 maai5 bat1. Can4 sin1 saang1 ge3 pou3 tau2 maai6 mei5 gwok3 bat1.
items.answer: ngo5 m4 soeng2 maai5 Can4 sin1 saang1 ge3 pou3 tau2 maai6 ge3 mei5 gwok3 bat1
items.answer_en: I don't want to buy the American pens that Mr. Chan's shop sells
items.hint: Turn the second sentence into a ge3 modifier before the noun

items.prompt: ngo5 hou2 soeng2 sik6 lung4 haa1. Ho4 taai2 zing2 lung4 haa1.
items.answer: ngo5 hou2 soeng2 sik6 Ho4 taai2 zing2 ge3 lung4 haa1
items.answer_en: I very much want to eat the lobster that Mrs. Ho makes
items.hint: Turn the second sentence into a ge3 modifier before the noun

exercises.title: Exercise 3
exercises.instructions: Choose from the following words to complete sentences a-d: san1 sin1 / mei5 gwok3 ge3 / jing1 gwok3 ge3 / sau2 tai4 / min5 fai3 / jat1 tou3 leng3 ge3 / gaai3 siu6 / hung4 sik1 / jyu4 gong2

items.prompt: _______ mit6 fo2 tung2 hou2 jau5 jung6.
items.answer_en: A portable fire extinguisher is very useful

items.prompt: Hai2 ni1 cyu3 jam2 seoi2 hai6 _______ ge3: nei5 m4 sai2 bei2 cin2.

exercises.title: Exercise 4
exercises.instructions: A creative test. Can you supply the cartoon caption in Cantonese? Mr Wong is saying: Don't be angry. I told you the fire extinguisher was a practical object.

items.prompt: Don't be angry. I told you the fire extinguisher was a practical object.
items.hint: Use m4 hou2 for don't, nau1 for angry, waa6 … teng1 / waa6 … zi1 for tell, and sat6 jung6 ge3 je5 for practical object

exercises.title: Have you understood?
exercises.instructions: Select the correct phrases from the ones in brackets (based on Dialogue 1).

notes.title: Typhoons
notes.body: It is likely that the word typhoon comes from the Cantonese word daai6 fung1 great wind. The summer monsoon season is the usual time for these swirling torrents of rain and ferocious winds which can exceed speeds of 160km/h, and woe betide those who are caught unprepared. In recent years few really bad typhoons have hit Hong Kong and early warning systems mean that there is usually plenty of time to get to safety and put up shutters. During a typhoon Hong Kong comes to a standstill, creating an unaccustomed silence which even the noise of the wind cannot disguise.
